title: Non-Abelian sheaf quantum LDPC codes: good and magical
authors: Zimu Li, Fuchuan Wei, Zhengyi Han, Zi-Wen Liu
abstract: Non-Abelian quantum codes connect quantum error correction, phases of matter, and computational resources. In this work, we develop a general framework for constructing non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes by gauging sheaf codes via cup products and use it to obtain families with constant encoding rate and linear distance. We resolve the coupled logical constraints using explicit representatives to characterize the full gauged code space. We provide a fundamental treatment of code distance based on the general Knill--Laflamme condition and combine expansion with cleaning to establish protection against arbitrary low-weight errors. We further construct an almost-good family whose entire code space exhibits long-range magic. Gauging and ungauging also enable logical Clifford measurements that prepare encoded magic states. These results extend good qLDPC codes beyond the Pauli stabilizer setting and provide a concrete foundation for exploring non-Abelian phases beyond geometric locality and pursuing the no low-energy trivial magic conjecture.
summary: This paper introduces a general framework for constructing advanced non-Abelian quantum LDPC codes by utilizing sheaf theory and cup products. It achieves codes with desirable parameters like constant rate and linear distance, extending error correction beyond standard Pauli stabilizers. These results offer a concrete theoretical tool for investigating non-Abelian topological phases and magic state generation.
main_problem: Developing and analyzing non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes to extend quantum error correction beyond the limitations of traditional Pauli stabilizer codes.
main_result: The authors constructed non-Abelian qLDPC codes with constant encoding rate and linear distance by gauging sheaf codes via cup products, providing a foundation for exploring non-Abelian phases.
method: The work employs advanced mathematical tools from algebraic topology, specifically gauging sheaf codes using cup products within a framework of cochain complexes.
model_or_system: The model involves non-Abelian quantum codes, which connect quantum error correction, phases of matter, and computational resources. The construction is based on generalizing sheaf codes using cell complexes.
key_observables: Code distance (characterized by the general Knill–Laflamme condition), encoding rate, and the presence of 'long-range magic' throughout the code space.
important_parameters: Constant encoding rate and linear distance ($	ext{[[N} \Theta(N), \Theta(N)]]$); the structure of the underlying cell complex $X$.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires moving beyond the traditional Pauli stabilizer setting and carefully handling logical constraints in the gauged code space.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general problem, develops the mathematical framework using sheaf theory and cup products, constructs the qLDPC codes, and analyzes their properties like distance and magic state preparation.
why_interesting: The extension of quantum error correction theory into non-Abelian structures and the connection to topological phases of matter is highly relevant for understanding robust quantum computation.
